answer_summary: Restoration peaked at 6.8 elements per hour after 11.6 hours; 95% of outages were restored after 182 hours, though the rate slowed late in the event.

answer_summary: A transmission-line fault triggered the simultaneous disconnection of about 1,500 MW of data-center load.

answer_summary: The concern arose from a very large simultaneous, unexpected load drop and the inherently rapid load changes of data-center facilities.

answer_summary: System voltage and frequency rose rapidly after the load disconnected, although the overall BES effect remained limited.

answer_summary: The 1,500 MW load loss created excess-generation imbalance comparable to suddenly adding a large nuclear unit; voltage and frequency rose, but total BES impact was limited.

answer_summary: Reliability planning needs better data-center behavior models and resources positioned to rebalance the grid rapidly after large load changes.

answer_summary: A single-line-to-ground fault on a 345 kV transmission circuit initiated the April 10 event.

answer_summary: Solar output fell because inverters tripped on loss of synchronization, ac overvoltage, and ac overcurrent.

answer_summary: Owners were told to coordinate with manufacturers on improved ride-through settings; implemented changes prevented repeat tripping and cut recovery to two or three minutes.

answer_summary: Extreme cold temperatures and freezing precipitation during February 8–20 initiated widespread generating-unit outages, derates, and failures to start.

answer_summary: Insufficient cold-weather preparedness and natural-gas supply interruptions reduced resource availability, with growing gas dependence worsening the fuel-supply impact.
